standards.title: Size full-height layouts with dvh and svh

standards.title: Cross to the JS thread only at thresholds

standards.title: Touch shared values only outside render
standards.rule: Read and write shared values only in worklets, handlers and effects, with .get() and .set() (functional form sv.set((v) => v + 1)); never during render and never through .value.
standards.why: A read during render is a snapshot that never updates and silently desyncs, a write fires mid-reconciliation and is replayed by re-renders you did not cause, and .value is the form the React Compiler cannot see through.

standards.rule: Switch between tabs with animation: 'none'; never slide between them.
standards.why: Tabs are peers, not a hierarchy; sliding implies depth that is not there, and the user pays for it dozens of times a session.

sources.evidence: Tab switches never slide; Never Ship: Sliding between tabs

standards.title: Back swipe mirrors custom transitions
standards.rule: Set animationMatchesGesture: true on every screen that sets a custom animation.
standards.why: It makes the iOS back swipe run the transition in reverse under the finger; otherwise dragging back looks like a different app than pushing forward.

sources.evidence: Screen transitions: animationMatchesGesture: true

standards.title: Design form sheets for Android's limits
standards.rule: Design form sheets for at most three detents, never rely on sheetGrabberVisible as the only sign that a sheet drags, keep the sheet a single screen (use presentation: 'modal' when it needs its own navigation), and give explicitly sized content to sheetAllowedDetents: 'fitToContents'.
standards.why: Android caps detents at three and silently truncates a longer array, shows no grabber, and cannot host native headers or nested stacks in a form sheet; a flex: 1 root has no intrinsic height to fit, so the detent is wrong.

values.fit: sheetAllowedDetents: 'fitToContents' with sized content, not a flex: 1 root

standards.title: Animate only transform and opacity in React Native
standards.rule: In React Native animate only transform and opacity, never width, height, margin, padding, flex, top, left or gap (collapse a header by translating content inside a fixed-height container with overflow: 'hidden'); the one exception is width on an absolutely positioned element with no children, such as a tab pill or a progress fill.
standards.why: Other properties re-run Yoga layout every frame for the node and its siblings, and animating a header's height competes with the scroll itself; an absolute, childless element re-lays-out nothing, and width keeps the corner radius that scaleX would smear.

values.never: width, height, margin, padding, flex, top, left, gap
values.exception: width on an absolutely positioned element with no children
values.indicator-sample: translateX and width with withTiming, duration 250, EASE_IN_OUT, measured once with onLayout

sources.evidence: 4. Pick the properties; Never Ship: Animating height / width / margin / flex / top

standards.title: Crossfade shadows and blur, never animate them
standards.rule: Never animate Android elevation or BlurView intensity; crossfade the opacity of a pre-shadowed or static blurred layer instead.
standards.why: Animating elevation re-renders the shadow every frame, and animating BlurView intensity re-renders the blur every frame on Android.

values.instead: opacity of a pre-shadowed layer or a static BlurView

standards.title: Translate before scale in transform arrays
standards.rule: Put translate before scale in a React Native transform array ([{ translateY }, { scale }]) unless you want the translate multiplied.
standards.why: transform is an array and order matters: reversed, the translate gets scaled too.

sources.evidence: 4. Pick the properties: transform is an array and order matters

standards.title: Never animate to a hardcoded height
standards.rule: Never animate to a hardcoded height; measure with onLayout, or animate a transform instead.
standards.why: allowFontScaling is on by default, so any height measured at the default type size is wrong at 200%.

standards.title: Spring when a finger is involved
standards.rule: Use a spring for any motion a finger started or can interrupt, and timing (an easing curve plus a duration) for everything else.
standards.why: Springs carry velocity through an interruption while timing curves restart, and a fixed-duration animation cannot respond to new input.

standards.title: Reanimated springs use duration and dampingRatio
standards.rule: Configure Reanimated springs with duration and dampingRatio from the source's table, never mass, stiffness and damping: { duration: 400, dampingRatio: 1 } for a default settle, { duration: 400, dampingRatio: 0.8, velocity } to reposition or snap back after a drag, { duration: 300, dampingRatio: 0.8, velocity } for sheets and drawers, plus overshootClamping: true wherever motion must not pass a hard edge; allow overshoot only when the gesture carried momentum.

standards.title: Reanimated curves are the custom beziers
standards.rule: In Reanimated use the source's custom curves and never the built-in easings or Easing.in: Easing.bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) for entering, exiting and by default, Easing.bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1) for movement on screen, Easing.bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1) for the iOS sheet curve, and linear only for constant motion such as progress.
standards.why: Reanimated's built-ins are as weak as CSS's, and ease-in starts slow, delaying the exact moment the user is watching.

standards.title: Mobile UI motion stays under 300ms
standards.rule: Keep React Native UI animations under 300ms: press feedback 100–150ms, toggles, chips and small state changes 150–200ms, sheets, modals and drawers a spring of about 300ms perceived, and toasts within the same 300ms cap; only navigation keeps the platform's longer default (iOS push 350ms).
standards.why: Mobile UI animations stay under 300ms, the same as web: match the platform for navigation and beat it everywhere else; a toast is uninvited, so it should be quicker and quieter than motion the user asked for.

standards.title: Grab from the current value, release with velocity
standards.rule: Start every drag from the element's current on-screen value (capture it in onStart) and hand the gesture's release velocity to the settling spring.
standards.why: Without the capture, grabbing a sheet mid-animation teleports it; with the velocity there is no seam between the finger releasing and the animation continuing, the single detail that most separates fluid from fine.

sources.evidence: onStart captures the current value; Velocity is handed to the spring

standards.title: Commit flicks by projected momentum
standards.rule: Decide whether a drag commits (dismiss, delete, snap) from its projected resting position, the current position plus project(velocity) using Apple's decay form ((velocity / 1000) * 0.998) / (1 - 0.998), so a quick flick commits; never use a distance-only threshold.
standards.why: A fast short swipe should commit and a slow long one should not; requiring 40% travel makes a sheet feel heavy, and the exponential-decay form is what Apple ships, not the v^2/2a from physics class.

sources.evidence: Two worklets you'll need everywhere; Velocity decides, not distance
Never Ship: Distance-only dismissal threshold

standards.title: Rubber-band drags past a boundary
standards.rule: Make boundaries resist instead of stopping dead: past an edge, move the element by rubberband(overshoot, dimension, 0.55) = (overshoot * dimension * 0.55) / (dimension + 0.55 * |overshoot|); a bottom sheet moves freely downward and resists upward past its top.
standards.why: The further past the edge, the less the element follows, the way real things slow before they stop; a hard stop reads as frozen.

sources.evidence: Two worklets you'll need everywhere; downward is free, upward past the top resists
Never Ship: Hard stop at a boundary

standards.title: Declare the pan axis inside scroll views
standards.rule: Give every pan gesture that shares space with a scroll view a movement threshold on its axis before it activates: activeOffsetX([-10, 10]) for a horizontal row swipe and activeOffsetY([-10, 10]) for a vertical sheet.
standards.why: With no axis declared a pan steals vertical scrolls and the list feels broken in a way that looks like a scrolling bug; the threshold lets the other direction win and requires intent before committing.

values.web-equivalent: ~10px movement threshold before committing to a direction

standards.title: Memoize gestures and animation builders
standards.rule: Wrap Gesture Handler v2 gestures in useMemo (on v3 use the hook form, which manages its own identity) and build layout-animation builders at module scope or in useMemo, never inline in JSX.
standards.why: Rebuilding a gesture on every render can reattach the recognizer and drop a drag that is mid-flight, and an inline builder chain rebuilds on every render.

standards.title: Never put entering on virtualized rows
standards.rule: Never put entering on a row inside FlatList, FlashList or any virtualized list; animate the list container once on mount, or use itemLayoutAnimation for reflow only.
standards.why: Rows are recycled, so the animation re-fires each time a row scrolls back into view and the list flickers while the user scrolls.

values.instead: animate the container once, or itemLayoutAnimation for reflow

standards.title: Clamp every scroll-driven interpolation
standards.rule: Drive scroll-linked motion from useAnimatedScrollHandler into a shared value (scrollEventThrottle={16}) and pass Extrapolation.CLAMP to every scroll-driven interpolate.
standards.why: Without CLAMP, scrolling past the input range keeps driving the output, so a header's opacity goes negative and it reappears inverted at the bottom of a long list.

standards.title: Follow the keyboard frame by frame
standards.rule: Move keyboard-following UI with react-native-keyboard-controller's useReanimatedKeyboardAnimation (translateY from its height, 0 to -keyboardHeight, on the UI thread), never with Keyboard.addListener plus a timing animation.
standards.why: The keyboard rides a private system curve and the event reaches the JS thread after the keyboard has started moving, so any duration visibly lags or leads it.

standards.title: Map haptics to the moment
standards.rule: Pick the expo-haptics call by moment: Haptics.selectionAsync() when a value ticks past a step (picker, slider detent, segmented control, tab press), impactAsync(Light) when something snaps home, a sheet detent catches, a drag commits or a pull crosses its refresh threshold, impactAsync(Medium) when a heavy object lands or a destructive action fires, and notificationAsync(Success or Error) when an operation succeeds or fails.
standards.why: Used sparingly, haptics make the app feel expensive; used everywhere, users turn them off.

standards.title: Fire haptics on the causal frame
standards.rule: Fire a haptic in the same frame as its visual, at the causal moment (the detent catching, the tab pressed), not when the animation finishes; from a worklet, schedule it with scheduleOnRN(Haptics.selectionAsync).
standards.why: A haptic that lags its animation reads as a glitch, not as feedback, and haptics must run on the React Native runtime.

standards.title: One haptic per user action
standards.rule: Fire at most one haptic per user action and only at meaningful moments (success, error, commit, snap); never on scroll, never per frame and never on an entrance animation the user did not cause.
standards.why: Over-feedback trains users to ignore all of it, and when haptics are everywhere users turn them off.

standards.title: Ship reduced motion with each RN animation
standards.rule: Ship reduced motion with each React Native animation (useReducedMotion(), or reduceMotion: ReduceMotion.System on the animation): keep the opacity and color changes that explain a state change, drop translation, scale, parallax and overshoot, and switch screen transitions to animation: 'fade'.
standards.why: Reduced motion means fewer and gentler, not zero, and it ships with the animation, not as a follow-up.

standards.title: Same press scale on iOS and Android
standards.rule: Use the Android ripple only in a Material-styled app; in a custom-designed app give both platforms the same press scale.
standards.why: The same scale on both platforms is more coherent than a ripple on one.

standards.title: React Native toasts leave the way they came
standards.rule: Make a React Native toast exit the way it entered, about 20% faster than its entrance and within the 300ms cap; the recipe enters with FadeInDown.duration(300).easing(EASE_OUT) and exits with FadeOutDown.duration(250).easing(EASE_OUT), both builders at module scope.
standards.why: Entering from the bottom and leaving to the side reads as two unrelated elements, and the arrival deserves the time while the departure does not because the user has finished reading.

sources.evidence: Toast: It exits the way it entered; Exit ~20% faster than entry; The 300ms cap holds here too

standards.title: Judge React Native motion on a release build
standards.rule: Judge React Native animation feel only on a release build on the slowest device you support, never in Expo Go, a dev build or the simulator, and feel-check it there by flicking it, interrupting it mid-flight, reversing it and running it on the slowest Android you have.
standards.why: A dev build's JS thread is slow enough to hide exactly the problems you are looking for, and gestures, velocity handoff and haptic timing cannot be judged from code.

values.checks: flick, interrupt mid-flight, reverse, slowest Android

sources.evidence: Hard Rules 5; Expo Go is not a performance environment; Never Ship: Judging feel in Expo Go or the simulator; Output

standards.why: Each fix has a why, and the same declaration is correct in one place and a defect in another; user-select: none on body text is a defect, on a button it is correct.
